 Salmonella Risk Prompts Recall of 365 Whole Foods Market Ashwagandha Capsules Sold in Stores and on Amazon 
 Vitality Works is recalling one lot of 365 Whole Foods Market ashwagandha capsules over possible Salmonella contamination. No illnesses were reported, but consumers should check the lot number and discard affected bottles. 
 Healthy Living 
 Salmonella Risk Prompts Recall of 365 Whole Foods Market Ashwagandha Capsules Sold in Stores and on Amazon
 Published Nov 01, 2026 9:15 AM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 MEHDI FEDOUACH | AFP via Getty Images 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Vitality Works Inc. of Albuquerque, New Mexico, is recalling one lot of 365 Whole Foods Market ashwagandha capsules because they may be contaminated with Salmonella . The recall was announced Oct. 30 and posted by the Food and Drug Administration .
 The capsules were sold at Whole Foods Market stores and online through Amazon.com from Nov. 24, 2025, through Oct. 20, 2026. That nearly 11-month window means bottles may already be sitting in medicine cabinets, gym bags, or kitchen drawers.
 No illnesses have been reported. But the company warned that Salmonella can cause "serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, frail or elderly people, and others with weakened immune systems," so households with the product should check the bottle now rather than finish it.
 One Lot, Two Ways It Was Sold
 The recall covers only 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules in the 120-count size. The product comes in a white plastic bottle.
 The recalled lot number is 2025-26227, with an expiration date of 10/13/2028. Both are printed on the bottom of the bottle. The notice lists the UPC as 9948252099. Bottles with a different lot number are not part of this recall.
 The notice lists 30 states and Washington, D.C., where the product was distributed: Arkansas, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, North Carolina, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, and Wyoming. Because the capsules were also sold on Amazon , buyers in other states should check their order history, too.
 Ashwagandha is an herb widely sold in supplements marketed for stress and sleep. Many people take it daily, which means a single contaminated lot can lead to repeated exposure for the same person.
 Routine Testing Caught It Before Any Reported Illness
 The potential contamination was identified through routine sampling of a single retail unit, the company said. The notice does not say who did the testing or how many bottles were sold.
 It also does not say whether other lots or other products made by Vitality Works were tested. As of the Oct. 30 notice, the recall had not been expanded, and no outbreak linked to the product had been announced.
 Herbal supplements have faced similar problems this year. In August, MedicalDaily reported on a recall of moringa capsules sold on Amazon after FDA testing of the raw moringa powder found Salmonella, before any illnesses were reported. Herbal products are made from dried plant material, and contamination at the farm or processing stage can carry into capsules.
 Supplements also do not go through the same review as medicines. Supplement makers are responsible for evaluating the safety and labeling of their products before marketing, and the FDA can act against unsafe products after they reach the market, according to the agency's dietary supplement guidance .
 The CDC estimates that Salmonella causes about 1.35 million infections in the United States every year, and only about 1 in 30 is diagnosed, according to the agency's Salmonella overview . Because most cases are never diagnosed, a lack of reported illness does not rule out that someone got sick.
 Salmonella Signs and the Family Members Most at Risk
 Healthy people infected with Salmonella often have fever, diarrhea that may be bloody, nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain, the recall notice said. Symptoms usually begin six hours to six days after infection and last four to seven days, according to the CDC .
 In rare cases, the bacteria can enter the bloodstream and cause more serious illness, including artery infections, infection of the heart lining, and arthritis.
 Risk is not equal across a household, which matters most in homes with young children or older relatives. The CDC says children under 5, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems are more likely to get seriously ill. Adults 50 and older with conditions such as heart disease also face higher risk.
 The CDC advises contacting a health care provider for diarrhea or vomiting that lasts more than two days, bloody stool or urine, a fever above 102 degrees, or signs of dehydration. Those signs include passing very little urine, dark urine, intense thirst , a dry mouth, dizziness, and, in children, crying without tears.
 Anyone who took the capsules should watch for symptoms and mention the exposure if they see a doctor.
 Refunds, Safe Disposal, and Supplement Safety Gaps
 The company says consumers should not take the recalled capsules. They should throw them away and not return them to the store. Refunds are available at any Whole Foods Market location.
 Customers who bought the product on Amazon can check their order history for the 120-count bottle and the purchase date. Questions can go to Vitality Works at (505) 268-9950, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mountain Time.
 People who take ashwagandha for stress or sleep and want to keep using it can ask a pharmacist or clinician about other options. It is also a good time to review all supplements in the home, since some can interact with prescription medicines.
 MedicalDaily will update this story if the recall expands or illnesses are reported. For now, the step is simple: flip the bottle over, check for lot 2025-26227, and if it matches, throw it away and get a refund.

 Key Questions Answered
 Which product is recalled? 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, 120 count, lot 2025-26227, expiration 10/13/2028.
 Where and when was it sold? At Whole Foods Market stores and on Amazon.com from Nov. 24, 2025, through Oct. 20, 2026. The notice lists 30 states and Washington, D.C.
 Has anyone gotten sick? No illnesses had been reported as of the Oct. 30 recall notice.
 What are the symptoms of Salmonella? Fever, diarrhea that may be bloody, nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain, usually starting six hours to six days after infection.
 Who is most at risk? Children under 5, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems.
 How do I get a refund? Throw the capsules away and request a refund at any Whole Foods Market store. Do not return the bottle.
